finding.claim: Request target is truncated at the first '#' before parsing, so query arguments after a raw '#' are never inspected in ARGS_GET.

trace.note: ExtractGetArguments receives only the truncated RawQuery

finding.guards_checked: No check exists that detects or handles a '#' in the request target; the truncation is unconditional. Backend-side parsing of '#' is assumed (Go net/http, PHP keep it in the query) and was not verified in this repo.

finding.claim: Query arguments beyond ArgumentLimit are silently dropped with only a debug log; no error flag is set, so rules cannot detect incomplete inspection.
finding.source: Query string with >= ArgumentLimit parameters (E2, transaction.go:761-765)

trace.note: debug warn only, then return; no tx variable set

finding.guards_checked: Limit is enforced (Len check) but the drop is silent; urlencoded body path (urlencoded.go:26-30) and multipart/JSON paths write directly to collections and bypass the limit entirely, so the limit is applied inconsistently.

finding.claim: JSON flattening writes res[objKey] with no collision check, so nested key a.b and literal key "a.b" collide and the later value silently overwrites the earlier one before inspection.
finding.source: JSON request body with colliding flattened keys (E4, json.go:32)

trace.note: objKey built by appending '.' and key
only the surviving value is copied to ARGS_POST

finding.guards_checked: No duplicate-key check; error from recursion limit is the only check and it does not cover collisions.

finding.claim: Duplicate Content-Type headers make the body processor (last header, via Set) and the MIME type passed to the processor (first header, via Get) disagree, so the body is parsed with the wrong processor or rejected.
finding.source: Two Content-Type request headers in attacker-chosen order (E3, transaction.go:376-390)
finding.sink: Body parsing in ProcessRequestBody (transaction.go:1091-1132) feeding multipart.go:25-31 or urlencoded.go:19-31

trace.note: second multipart header overwrites processor to MULTIPART (last wins)
ParseMediaType on the first header value; returns 'not a multipart body' error when it is urlencoded

finding.guards_checked: No rejection of duplicate Content-Type headers. Assumes collections Get returns values in insertion order (not read in this audit). Exploitability depends on the backend accepting duplicate Content-Type headers.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI fails, the error branch never extracts query arguments, so ARGS and QUERY_STRING stay empty for the whole request.
finding.source: Request target with invalid percent-escape or control byte (E1, transaction.go:819-834)

trace.note: ParseRequestURI returns error for e.g. '%zz' in path

finding.guards_checked: urlencodedError is set but nothing in the engine acts on it; a rule would have to read it explicitly. Go net/http rejects such targets before the WAF, so this needs a connector that forwards them.

finding.claim: Multipart file parts have no count or size limit (UploadFileLimit is set but never read; RequestBodyNoFilesLimit is a TODO), and each file's temp file handle is held open until the function returns via defer in the loop. Fd exhaustion makes CreateTemp fail, ProcessRequest aborts, and later parts are never inspected while rules still run on the partial body.
finding.source: Multipart body with thousands of small file parts (E4, multipart.go:58-64)
finding.sink: os.CreateTemp per file part (multipart.go:64) and body-parse abort feeding rule evaluation (transaction.go:1136-1141)

trace.note: os.CreateTemp per file part, no count check
defer temp.Close() inside loop holds each fd until return
CreateTemp failure sets strict error and returns
Rules.Eval still runs on the partial body after processor error
UploadFileLimit field exists but has no reader in internal/

finding.guards_checked: UploadFileLimit and RequestBodyNoFilesLimit are unenforced (grep of internal/ shows no reads). Blocking depends on a rule reacting to REQBODY_ERROR; without one the remaining parts are uninspected. Total bytes are bounded by RequestBodyLimit (transaction.go:950-961).

finding.claim: Temp file created for a file part is not registered in filesTmpNames when io.Copy fails with a non-EOF error, so Transaction.Close never removes it and the file is leaked on disk.
finding.source: File part whose body read or temp write fails with a non-EOF error (E4, multipart.go:70-79)
finding.sink: Temp file on disk under UploadDir (multipart.go:64); removal path Close (transaction.go:1681-1685) is skipped

trace.note: non-EOF error returns before filesTmpNames.Add at line 79
Close removes only files registered in filesTmpNames

finding.guards_checked: ErrUnexpectedEOF is handled (line 76). Reachability of a non-EOF copy error from the network was not confirmed; severity is low unless it is reachable.
